what: A new ordered-dither family for web/shaders/dither: 'mix' modes that mix up to 16 palette colours per pixel in linear light, and the checks that decide whether it replaces bayer4 as the default
fixed_before_first_run: 2026-10-11, after the diagnosis and before any mix-mode code ran

why.judge_result: Model judges preferred a plain per-channel Bayer 4 x 4 EGA dither over raw-native's bayer4 on 12 of 12 trials (evidence/shaders-model-judges-2026-10-10.json).
why.diagnosis: Looked at side by side (panel images, 2026-10-11): raw-native's pair dither turns the dark green hills and the warm floor grey and the purple ridge saturated blue, while the per-channel dither keeps each region's hue. Cause: orderedPick mixes only the two palette colours that bracket the pixel along one segment, so a colour between three or more palette entries (most colours on EGA) falls back to a grey or wrong-hue pair; and it sets the mix fraction by projection in OKLab, while the eye averages a dither in linear light, so darks rise (lab-2 step 15: a ramp at 20 shows as 57). The old modes stay bit-equal to the author's retro-dither.js (M1 criterion 10) and are not changed.

method: Per pixel: start from the colour in linear light and an error of zero; 16 times, take the palette colour nearest in OKLab to the colour plus the error (clamped to [0, 1]), add it to a plan, and add the colour minus that palette colour (linear) to the error. Sort the plan by the palette colour's OKLab L, ties by index. The ordered threshold t (Bayer 4, Bayer 8 or the blue-noise mask, folded toward 0.5 by strength) picks entry floor(16 t). Modes: mix-bayer4, mix-bayer8, mix-blue. Strength 0 picks the nearest colour. Brightness must be 0 (refused otherwise). The plan idea follows pattern dithering (a list of candidates whose mean matches the colour, ordered by lightness); the code is written here.

bounds.gpu_parity: palette index per pixel against the f64 CPU reference: at most 0.001% of pixels differ per case (2 of the random plate's 262,144), cases = every palette in [gameboy, cga, ega, pico8, nes, mono1] x every mix mode x both parity plates, strength 1, plus pico8 mix-bayer4 at strength 0.7
bounds.quality: Low-pass error: the output and the source each box-filtered 4 x 4 in linear light (stride 1, clamped edges), then the mean OKLab distance x 100 over all pixels. mix-bayer4 must be strictly lower than both bayer4 (the current default) and a per-channel Bayer 4 x 4 baseline (each sRGB channel offset by (t - 0.5) / 3, then the nearest palette colour in sRGB; the generic method the competitor shader uses, written here) on every frame and palette: frames = the two panel frames (scene card 320 x 180 and gameFrame 320 x 240 at t = 0.5, sRGB), testCard 256 x 224, gradientPlate 320 x 180, the street fixture 480 x 300 (sRGB-encoded); palettes = ega and pico8. 20 comparisons; all must hold. On the two panel frames with EGA the competitor's own renders (D:/shader-work/panel/out) are scored too and mix-bayer4 must be lower there as well.
bounds.default_rule: mix-bayer4 becomes the default mode (createGpuDither, ditherRef and the post pass when mode is omitted) only if every quality comparison holds and the re-judge below does not record 'lost' against bayer4-ega. Otherwise the default stays bayer4 and the result is recorded as it stands.

rejudge_protocol.authority: The author's instruction, verbatim, 2026-10-10: "I want you to be the blind judge" (the amendment in evidence/shaders-model-judges-2026-10-10.json). Same design as that amendment.
rejudge_protocol.pairs: raw-native mix-bayer4 vs bayer4-ega and raw-native mix-blue vs bluenoise-ega, on the same two frames (scene card 320 x 180, gameFrame 320 x 240), the competitor images unchanged from panel 1; shown nearest-neighbour x3 as before. 4 pairs, each twice with sides swapped: 8 trials per judge. Question unchanged: 'Which is the better picture, reduced to these 16 colours?'
rejudge_protocol.judges: Three fresh model agents with no conversation context; each sees only a folder of anonymised images and a trials file. No judge sees the key, the code or any report.
rejudge_protocol.blinding: Image ids are random. The key is written to D:/shader-work/judge3/key.json and its sha256 committed in evidence/shaders-dither-mix-runs.json before any judge starts. The vote files are hashed before the key is opened.
rejudge_protocol.metric_and_rule: Unchanged: win rate with a 95% Wilson interval per competitor, pooled over judges; 'preferred' when the lower bound is above 0.5, 'lost' when the upper bound is below 0.5, else 'not distinguishable'.
rejudge_protocol.limits: The judges are the same model family that built the shader, so shared biases can favour the same look; a model preference is not a human preference; repeats are near copies, so the intervals are too narrow; three judges is a small panel.

does_not_prove: Preference by people; quality on palettes other than EGA and PICO-8; temporal stability (a 16-entry plan can flip on a slow ramp in motion; not measured here).
